baslik: Principle wants companies to stop predicting the future — and start simulating it
metin:
What if, instead of trying to predict the future, companies could simulate hundreds of versions of it — and work out what they would do in each one?

That’s the premise behind Principle, an AI-powered strategic simulation platform that builds digital models of organisations, competitors, regulators, and other market forces, then plays out hundreds of plausible futures to stress-test strategic decisions.

Its founder, entrepreneur Artur Kiulian, is adamant that Principle isn't trying to build a crystal ball.

“We're not really building a prediction machine. We're building an action machine.”

It’s a distinction shaped by Kiulian’s own experience of events few organisations were adequately prepared for — from COVID-19 to Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine — and by his subsequent work using AI for crisis response and government decision-making.

Now Principle is applying that thinking to corporate strategy, helping companies model everything from competitor moves and market expansion to geopolitical shocks — and explore what they could do before those futures

Not only that, but something happens that renders all of his car’s and phone’s technology useless; everything he has taken for granted is no longer particularly or practically useful. 

He has no idea how to get back to his wife and friends at a place he had no trouble finding when his tech worked, but there is something more profound going on. George has not forgotten how to drive; he has forgotten how to navigate without the machinery doing most of the thinking for him.

baslik: PlantVoice is bringing ‘plant intelligence’ to precision agriculture
metin:
Traditionally, farmers make decisions based on weather forecasts, soil moisture measurements, visual observations, and their own experience in the field. These are valuable sources of information, but they only provide part of the picture. Italian startup PlantVoice, however, believes that the plant is the most reliable indicator of its own needs. PlantVoice has developed an agronomic platform specifically designed for food production, integrating real-time plant physiological data with weather and soil data. It aims to make "plant intelligence", a standard layer within modern agriculture — a future where every important agronomic decision is supported not only by environmental data, but by direct feedback from the plant itself.

I spoke to the COO, Giorgia Ferrari, to learn more.

Listening to the plant, not just the environment

PlantVoice was founded in 2023 by Matteo Beccatellia, a chemist who studied biosensors in Parma and the US, and Tommaso Beccatellia, who has a background in manufacturing and 3D-printed objects.

PlantVoice has developed a biocompatible sensor head made from a specific wood fibre to match the plant's components.

Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), a group of lung diseases that cause breathing problems, is another major burden. Around 1.7 million people in the UK have COPD, while many others are living with the condition without knowing it. The diagnosis gap is significant. At least 600,000 people in the UK are currently waiting for a formal COPD diagnosis, while many healthcare providers lack the capacity to meet demand for diagnostic testing.

baslik: ICEYE adds predictive flood modeling through partnership with The Water Institute
metin:
ICEYE is partnering with The Water Institute to combine satellite-based flood observations with predictive flood modeling for governments, insurers and emergency management organizations in the US. ICEYE operates a large synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite constellation and provides flood mapping and impact data, while The Water Institute developed FloodID, a platform that uses hydrologic models, AI, Earth observation data and cloud computing to forecast how floods may develop over time. As part of the partnership, FloodID and its core development team will move to ICEYE, with former FloodID lead Hugh J. Roberts joining ICEYE as Head of Predictive Intelligence. The companies will integrate FloodID’s forecasts with ICEYE’s satellite observations so that predictions can be updated as new imagery becomes available during a flood, with the aim of providing a single operational view of observed and expected flood conditions.
